note: The main banks: Bancolombia, Davivienda, Banco de Bogotá and BBVA Colombia, the largest issuers of credit cards. Bancolombia: every personal credit card with its own page, each read on 2026-10-30 (13 cards: Mastercard Clásica, Oro, Platinum, Black, Joven and Ideal; Visa Clásica, Oro, Platinum and Infinite; American Express Green, Gold and Platinum): purchases and cash advances at 2.1155% a month (28.5582% effective a year), written as the monthly rate; the monthly handling fee (cuota de manejo) after any introductory months, from 17,250 pesos (Joven) to 50,960 (Black, Infinite, Amex Platinum). The months free for a card applied for online, the Clásica's year free for 695,000 pesos of purchases a month (introductory, kept as the earlier reading said) and the Amex Green's 50% exemption aren't written; the pages carry an Imperva script but served their full content to a plain request, as on 2026-10-29. Davivienda: its own card pages are behind an Incapsula check and weren't used; the RappiCard, a credit card Banco Davivienda issues, publishes a monthly tariff sheet (in force 1 to 31 October 2026): purchases, cash advances and default interest all at 2.1176% a month (28.59% effective a year), written as rate, cash rate and penalty rate; no handling fee; international purchases 2.50% (the sheet sets the figure against both the bank's own commission and the network's conversion charge, read as the whole foreign fee); a cash advance at a national machine 12,000 pesos (abroad nothing, digital advances 7,000); collection charges from 11 to 30 days late of 1.30% of the overdue balance, at most 200,000 pesos, written as the late fee (5.80% from 31 to 60 days and 12% from 61 to 180 aren't modelled). Banco de Bogotá's and BBVA Colombia's card pages answered 403 (an error page), so neither is written. No minimum payment is published for Bancolombia's and Davivienda's cards; tried (wave 5, 30 October 2026): every document this file cites, downloaded again on 30 October 2026 and searched for a minimum payment, states none for them; no web search was made for them in this wave, the searches shared by every agent having gone to the larger countries; archive.org's availability API, asked for each of the 14 documents this file cites, names a snapshot for 13 of them, which can't be read, web.archive.org being refused from here.
